shots.body: A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with a 135mm lens from inside a dark staff room at night, looking out through a rain-streaked sash window. The blurred window bar and running raindrops on the glass cut across the near foreground, out of focus. Across a narrow street, sharp and large in the frame, is the brick wall of a flat above a shuttered café. An estate agent's board, fixed flat to the wall and facing the camera, fills a third of the frame. The board is plain red with one word on it in very large bold white capital letters: "SOLD". There is no other writing on it. A man's gloved hand and a cordless drill are at its top corner, the rest of him out of frame on a ladder whose top two rungs show. Beside the board is the flat's dark sash window with one pot plant on the sill inside, and nothing else. One light source only, no fill: one orange street lamp below and to the left, raking up the wet brick. The window of the flat is black.

A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with a 50mm lens resting on a staff-room table at dusk, looking up. The open pages of a small building-society passbook and a stub of pencil fill the near foreground, out of focus. Above them Denise sits close, leaning over the book, her eyes down on the page and her lips slightly parted as she counts, one finger on a line. Behind her is a row of dented steel lockers with a coat on a hook, and nothing else. One light source only, no fill: the last blue dusk from a window out of frame on the right, on the near side of her face. The far side of her face and the lockers fall into black.

A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with a 35mm lens low on the wet pavement of a narrow British street at night, looking straight across the road at a shop front, square on. The kerb and a puddle fill the near foreground, out of focus. Across the road a small kebab shop is the only lit shop in a row of shuttered ones. Above its window runs a wide, flat shop sign board, facing the camera: a plain deep dark-blue painted board, completely blank, with no lettering, no logo and no picture anywhere on it, and a row of bare clear light bulbs along its top edge. There is no writing anywhere in the picture. Through the steamed-up window, soft, a doner spit turns and one man stands behind the counter. Bin bags by the door. The only light is the row of bulbs and the shop window under it, reflected in the wet road. Everything else is black.

A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with an 18mm lens on the tarmac of a street at dusk, looking up at a load being wheeled past. A hand pallet truck carrying a wooden pallet stacked high with shrink-wrapped blocks of paper crosses the middle of the frame, its steel forks and small wheels close to the lens in the near foreground, out of focus. Mr Blue hauls the handle at the left, walking backwards, and Mr Red pushes the stack from the right; both are red in the face with their mouths open, shouting at each other over the top of the load. Behind them a steel crowd barrier and the turned backs of a crowd run across the frame, out of focus, under a dark dusk sky with drifting pink and blue smoke, and nothing else. One light source only, no fill: one red hand flare burning in the crowd behind them on the left. The near sides of their faces are in shadow.

A frame from a feature film, shot on 35mm with a 24mm lens resting on a television studio desk, looking up. Two water glasses and a desk microphone stand in the near foreground, out of focus. Behind the desk Mr Blue and Mr Red stand close together with an arm round each other's shoulders like old friends, ties loosened, both grinning straight into the lens, Mr Blue slightly nearer and larger. Crumpled script pages lie on the desk. Behind them is a dark studio with one television camera whose tally light is off, and nothing else. One light source only, no fill: one hard studio lamp high on the right. The left side of both faces falls into deep shadow.

A frame from a home video shot at night on a cheap standard-definition digital camcorder held at arm's length, with its small built-in light switched on. Mr Red and Mr Blue fill the frame, too close to the lens, arms round each other's necks, ties loosened, heads back, singing with their mouths wide open, faces shiny and slightly blown out by the camera's light, their eyes catching it. The frame is tilted and cuts off the top of one head. Behind them in the dark, lit only by spill, The Presenter laughs with a champagne glass raised and The Proprietor sits alone in a chair staring into the lens, not smiling. Further back, the pale wall of a marquee, a string of bulbs and a chocolate fountain, soft and noisy. One light source only: the camcorder's own harsh white light, falling off within two metres into grainy black. Low resolution, video noise in the shadows, smeared highlights, washed colour. 16:9. Thanks
